correctness.rationale: With hubs first the even powers of H restrict on the hubs to powers of BB*, and the odd powers contribute zero there. BB* has diagonal m and (v,u) entry S, with spectral values m±s. For s>0 the (v,u) entries of the two projectors are ±S/(2s), fixing the conjugation and normalization in the cosine difference. At s=0 it is a scalar Gram matrix; at s=m one frequency is zero and t=π/√(2m) gives unit magnitude. In the interior, unit magnitude requires opposite cosine extrema. Reducing the ratio of the corresponding positive integer multiples of π preserves opposite parity; conversely reduced opposite parity gives the displayed time. A reduced both-odd ratio is periodic with no such time, so its maximum is strictly below one. For irrational R, take t=(2k+1)π/√(m−s); the other argument runs over a dense irrational rotation modulo 2π, so one can approach the pair of extrema at positive times. At R=3 the probability is 4y(1−y)² for y=cos²(t√(m−s)), giving the attained maximum 16/27 at y=1/3. The increasing radius map is a bijection onto the interior; rationals of both parity types densely approximate every R by large denominators of prescribed parity, with reduction preserving the type. The connected phase torus attains s=0 via roots of unity and s=m via alignment, and therefore all radii. Its analytic s² is globally nonconstant and hence nonconstant in every open box. Each such box contains a connected smaller box with a nontrivial range of s², so every dense radius class pulls back densely. Individual level sets of nonconstant analytic s² have measure zero; the countably many excluded radii thus leave full measure for the irrational-ratio phase class. The result concerns the ideal fixed closed Hamiltonian, not transfer in a bounded observation window.
residual_risks: PGST is an unbounded-time assertion; recurrence times and phase robustness at finite time are not certified.

originality.rationale: The established parts are the two-frequency mechanism, the Hermitian phase-matching criteria, and even the coherent magnetic-square amplitude as an immediate consequence of an earlier square block decomposition. The surviving claim is their exact realization and classification over the arbitrary unit-phase assignments of the entire K_{2,m} family: all loop-phase dependence on this marked hub pair is compressed into its phasor resultant (up to the output phase), with a full phase-space classification. The inspected statements do not supply that network-specific reduction and pullback; neither the arithmetic technique nor the 3:1 two-mode maximization is credited as a new technique or independent phenomenon.
residual_risks: Specialized closed magnetic-square literature may fully articulate the reduced parity regimes or the same resonant ceiling. The pass is for the resultant-controlled arbitrary-phase classification on K_{2,m}, not an assertion of priority for all equivalent two-frequency dynamics.

value.rationale: For a natural multi-path network this replaces all independent magnetic phases for the marked transport problem by one measurable interference parameter, while keeping coupling magnitudes fixed. It gives an exact design and obstruction criterion rather than a single calibrated example: phase-only tuning has dense but null exact-transfer and blocked classes, alongside almost-everywhere arbitrarily good transfer that need not be exact. The all-phase statement and its strong distinction between topology and measure are useful for analyzing coherent phase sensitivity; the elementary resonance maximum alone would not meet this value standard.
residual_risks: This phase-space geometry is not a guarantee of small transfer times or of performance with decoherence, noisy couplings, or uncertainty over a fixed time horizon.
